records.title: Small Talk
records.creator: The Etherington Brothers
records.collection: How to Think When You Write
subject: small-talk
conversation
dialogue
social-rhythm
records.notes:
Lane: DIALOGUE_RHYTHM
KFB research notes are derived authoring guidance, not a claim that the tutorial visual has been inspected in isolation.
principles: Use low-stakes dialogue as social telemetry rather than filler.
Anchor ambient lines to relationship, activity, place, mood or local observation.

records.title: Speech Patterns
records.creator: The Etherington Brothers
records.collection: How to Think When You Write
subject: speech-patterns
character-voice
dialogue
records.notes:
Lane: CHARACTER_VOICE
KFB research notes are derived authoring guidance, not a claim that the tutorial visual has been inspected in isolation.
principles: Differentiate voice through worldview, sociolect, cadence and response habits.
Avoid solving character voice with catchphrase repetition.

records.title: Tics and Tells
records.creator: The Etherington Brothers
records.collection: How to Think When You Write
subject: tics
tells
nonverbal-language
character-detail
records.notes:
Lane: NONVERBAL_BEHAVIOR
KFB research notes are derived authoring guidance, not a claim that the tutorial visual has been inspected in isolation.
principles: Treat recurring nonverbal behavior as meaning-bearing and selectively triggered.
Route performance cues to gesture/gaze/micro-motion without making them state owners.

records.title: Interrupt a Scene
records.creator: The Etherington Brothers
records.collection: How to Think When You Write
subject: interruptions
conversation
scene-rhythm
dialogue
records.notes:
Lane: CONVERSATION_FLOW
KFB research notes are derived authoring guidance, not a claim that the tutorial visual has been inspected in isolation.
principles: Use interruption to reveal power, urgency, intimacy, fear or avoidance.
The interrupted speaker's response is part of the beat.

records.title: Silence Is Golden
records.creator: The Etherington Brothers
records.collection: How to Think When You Write
subject: silence
pause
negative-space
dialogue-rhythm
records.notes:
Lane: DIALOGUE_RHYTHM
KFB research notes are derived authoring guidance, not a claim that the tutorial visual has been inspected in isolation.
principles: Silence, gaze, gesture and pause are valid authored outputs.
Do not manufacture dialogue because a Resident is present.

records.title: The 4th Wall
records.creator: The Etherington Brothers
records.collection: How to Think When You Write
subject: fourth-wall
audience-address
meta-narration
records.notes:
Lane: META_NARRATION
KFB research notes are derived authoring guidance, not a claim that the tutorial visual has been inspected in isolation.
principles: Use meta-address rarely and only when the relationship to audience/player is earned.
Meta narration should add framing, not dissolve Kayfabe into generic self-awareness.

records.title: Failure
records.creator: The Etherington Brothers
records.collection: How to Think When You Write
subject: failure
character-reveal
response-to-setback
records.notes:
Lane: FAILURE_REACTION
KFB research notes are derived authoring guidance, not a claim that the tutorial visual has been inspected in isolation.
principles: Use failure to reveal character, changed expectations and social consequence.
Repeated failure should increase specificity and memory, not merely joke intensity.

records.title: Excuses
records.creator: The Etherington Brothers
records.collection: How to Think When You Write
subject: excuses
rationalization
character-reveal
subtext
records.notes:
Lane: FAILURE_REACTION
KFB research notes are derived authoring guidance, not a claim that the tutorial visual has been inspected in isolation.
principles: Treat self-justification as subtext and character revelation.
Distinguish what is said from what is meant and wanted.

records.title: The Group Dynamic
records.creator: The Etherington Brothers
records.collection: How to Think When You Write
subject: group-dynamic
ensemble
social-pressure
multiple-characters
records.notes:
Lane: GROUP_REACTION
KFB research notes are derived authoring guidance, not a claim that the tutorial visual has been inspected in isolation.
principles: Select a primary respondent in group events instead of making everyone speak.
Use status, relationship, proximity and stake to decide who reacts verbally.

records.collection: How to Think When You Write
subject: local-colour
setting
voice

records.notes:
Lane: LOCAL_VOICE
KFB research notes are derived authoring guidance, not a claim that the tutorial visual has been inspected in isolation.
principles: Let place/faction change vocabulary, examples, norms and social register.
Avoid decorative dialect or jargon pasted onto generic lines.

records.notes:
Lane: MEMORY_CALLBACK
KFB research notes are derived authoring guidance, not a claim that the tutorial visual has been inspected in isolation.
